entities.summary: The Musée de l'Homme is an anthropology museum in Paris, France. It was established in 1937 by Paul Rivet for the 1937 Exposition Internationale des Arts et Techniques dans la Vie Moderne. It is the descendant of the Musée d'Ethnographie du Trocadéro, founded in 1878. The Musée de l'Homme is a research center under the authority of various ministries, and it groups several entities from the CNRS. The Musée de l'Homme is one of the seven departments of the Muséum national d'histoire naturelle. The Musée de l'Homme occupies most of the Passy wing of the Palais de Chaillot in the 16th arrondissement.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Musée de l'Homme played a crucial role in promoting anthropology and human sciences in France during the mid-20th century. Its collection of over 2 million artifacts has contributed significantly to the field of anthropology, making it one of the leading institutions in Europe.
